subject: HlthWise demo — commitments, open questions, and test plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@hlthwise.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + agreed next steps from today’s demo

Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and so your security & infra teams have something to look at.

Key pain points you shared
- Latency spikes during daily clinical-note bulk processing windows (p95 frequently > 850ms).
- Unpredictable inference cost when usage bursts hit peaks (hard to budget).
- Data residency + HIPAA compliance constraints for PHI in New York care lines.
- Need for a short pilot that proves both performance and cost predictability before procurement.

What we demonstrated
- Redwood hosted + dedicated capacity options; example rollout from hosted -> dedicated for burst isolation.
- Latency controls (autoscaling policies) and prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token cost.
- Private deployment pattern and KMS integration options (we noted KMS/HSM compatibility).

Agreed next steps (from us)
1) Run two head-to-head tests you requested:
   a. Throughput durability test — simulated burst profile: 1k concurrent inference bursts over 30-minute window; measure p50/p95/p99 latency and error rate.
   b. Quality/regression test — 500 annotated clinical notes run through Redwood and the incumbent (CloudModelX) to verify parity on extraction accuracy and hallucination rate.
2) Provide a Mutual Action Plan (attached) with milestones and a proposed PoC contract term for review.
3) Share security artifacts and answer initial compliance questions (see short checklist in the MAP).

Open questions we still need from HlthWise
- Exact SSO/IdP contact for setting up a sandbox (SAML/Okta?).
- Expected dataset size for the quality run (samples and redaction guidance).
- Any additional monitoring requirements beyond latency (e.g., token-level cost attribution per route).

Attachments included: hlthwise_poc_scope.pdf (PoC scope), mutual-action-plan.xlsx, hlthwise_sample_payload.json (anonymized sample).

Proposed timings
- Start throughput test the week of 11/16 if infra provisioning is ready.
- Full scorecard and decision matrix by 11/22.

If that aligns, I’ll ask Dev to provision the test cluster and Mateo to own the comparison scorecard. Thanks again — I’ll loop in security contacts once you confirm who that should be.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

  * Two model configs: (1) full-precision variant (baseline) and (2) 8-bit quantized variant with identical accuracy knobs.
  * Monitoring endpoints for p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, and per-route token count.
  * Token cost reporting (per-minute aggregation) exported to the PoC Drive folder.
- ETA: can you confirm provisioning timeline? The customer wants to start 11/16.

- Run the 500-sample quality comparison against CloudModelX and Redwood. Produce a simple scorecard: accuracy, hallucination rate, latency, and cost per inference.
- Deliverable: spreadsheet + short one-pager with recommendation by 11/22.

Attachments: hlthwise_poc_scope.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx, hlthwise_sample_payload.json.

Thanks — shout if any of that is unrealistic.

—Hannah
